title: Contributing to decisionfacets
text: Open issue first discuss change, unless small fix (typos, documentation). Fork repository create branch change. Follow existing style: base R Imports, df_ function prefix, roxygen2 documentation runnable @examples. Add update tests tests/test-core.R. New statistical methods come known-truth check (simulate model, recover truth); see inst/validation/ pattern used throughout package. title: Decision Accuracy and Consistency for Rater-Mediated Exams
text: 1,000 candidates, 4 items, 12 raters (severity SD 0.6), 2 raters per candidate, cut = mean rating 2. Means 100 replications: Raw totals: 176 truly rater-dependent candidates per 1,000. TAM flags 169, recovering 71% true flags (75% TAM’s flags real). oracle true parameters also recovers 71%, remaining gap measurement error 8 ratings per candidate, estimation error. Expected misclassifications per 1,000: 160 raw totals (116 measurement, 44 rater assignment) versus 117 measure rule (assignment 1). TAM estimates: 160 / 116 / 44. Realized errors simulation: 160. measure-based fair-average rules, candidate flagged rater-dependent.

what: One examiner per case, scores 0-100 (development version)
title: Decision Accuracy and Consistency for Rater-Mediated Exams
text: 400 candidates; 6 12 cases , scored one examiner per case; examiner severity SD 2, 4 6 score points; 4 10 qualified examiners per case; residual SD 8; pass mean score reaches 70. 50 replications per condition (600 data sets; inst/validation/assignment_study.R): Severity spread drives everything (explains 70% variance number examiner-dependent candidates). Twelve cases dilute examiner effects six, fewer candidates depend examiners. Examiner severities recovered correlation 0.84-0.99 (lowest examiners barely differ) RMSE 1 point; residual SD estimated 7.9 (true 8). Expected misclassifications calibrated: differ actually occurred -0.3 per data set average, estimated examiner component within 0.2 truth. Severity-adjusted scoring (measure, fair_average) removes examiner dependence entirely. Individual flags harder two-rater panels: many examiners per candidate examiner effect one decision small relative measurement error, estimates find 31-58% truly examiner-dependent candidates, 60-71% flags correct. program-level decomposition remains accurate.

title: Decision Accuracy and Consistency for Rater-Mediated Exams
text: Current limits: crossed designs need equal panel sizes; missing ratings within candidate’s assignment; severity (halo drift terms); continuous model uses single residual SD examiners ignores bounds score scale. ratings per person, JMLE stretches logit scale (~15% validation); prefer TAM.

what: Define a pass/fail cut under an explicit decision rule — df_cut
title: Define a pass/fail cut under an explicit decision rule — df_cut
text: decision rule determines rater severity can reach decision: `raw_total` Pass summed observed ratings reach `value`.     Severity passes straight decision. `raw_mean` Pass mean observed rating reaches `value` (    example 70 0-100 scale). Equivalent `raw_total` cut     `value` times number ratings, convenient     candidates different numbers ratings. `measure` Pass severity-adjusted measure reaches `value`     (logits ordinal scores; score points continuous scores).     Severity modeled ; effect measurement precision     remains. `fair_average` Pass FACETS-style fair average (expected     mean rating per cell average rater) reaches `value`.     monotone measure, behaves like `measure`     transformed cut. continuous scores equals measure.

title: Fit a many-facet measurement model — df_fit
text: Ordinal scores fitted many-facet Rasch rating scale model; continuous scores (see [df_data()]) linear many-facet model `score = theta - delta - lambda + error`, `error ~ N(0, sigma^2)`.

title: Fit a many-facet measurement model — df_fit
code: df_fit(data, engine = NULL, max_iter = 1000, tol = NULL)

title: Fit a many-facet measurement model — df_fit
text: data `df_data` object. engine ordinal scores: `"tam"` (marginal ML via `TAM::tam.mml.mfr`, default TAM installed) `"jmle"` (built-joint maximum likelihood, FACETS approach). continuous scores: `"linear"` (least squares; option). max_iter, tol Convergence controls; `tol = NULL` uses engine's default (1e-4 TAM, 1e-6 JMLE linear).

title: Fit a many-facet measurement model — df_fit
text: `df_fit` object: `$data`, `$par` (named `theta`, `delta`,   `lambda`, `tau` ordinal `sigma` `model = "linear"`   continuous scores; TAM linear also `theta_prior`, population   mean SD), `$engine`, `$converged`, `$iterations`, TAM   fitted `$model`.

title: Fit a many-facet measurement model — df_fit
text: engines report item difficulties rater severities   centered 0. Ordinal person measures logit scale (EAPs   TAM); continuous person measures score scale, measure   expected rating average-severity rater average item. rating network must connected: every rater must linked every   shared candidates items, severities   comparable. `df_fit()` stops . JMLE person measures clamped [-7, 7], extreme scores get   finite arbitrary measure. JMLE's known small-sample spread inflation   corrected. linear model ignores bounds score scale   (e.g. 0 100), matters many ratings sit bound.

title: Fit a many-facet measurement model — df_fit
code: sim <- df_simulate(n_persons = 200, n_items = 3, n_raters = 6, seed = 1) fit <- df_fit(sim$data, engine = "jmle") cor(fit$par$lambda, sim$par$lambda[names(fit$par$lambda)]) #> [1] 0.9958962 # \donttest{ if (requireNamespace("TAM", quietly = TRUE)) {   fit_tam <- df_fit(sim$data, engine = "tam")   fit_tam$par$tau } #> [1] -1.6106372 -0.5208191  0.5767848  1.5546715 # }

title: Simulate a rater-mediated administration with known truth — df_simulate
text: Two scoring designs available. `"crossed"` design candidate scored every item panel `raters_per_person` raters drawn random pool. `"per_item"` design item (example oral-examination case) set `raters_per_item` qualified examiners, candidate's items scored one examiner drawn item's set, examiner scoring candidate twice can avoided.

title: Simulate a rater-mediated administration with known truth — df_simulate
text: n_persons, n_items, n_raters Facet sizes. raters_per_person Panel size per candidate (crossed design). n_cat Number score categories (ordinal scores 0..n_cat-1). theta_mean, theta_sd Candidate ability distribution (ordinal: logits). item_sd, severity_sd SDs item difficulty rater severity (centered). continuous scores score scale. tau Category thresholds; defaults equally spaced [-1.5, 1.5]. design `"crossed"` `"per_item"`. raters_per_item Qualified examiners per item per-item design (default: raters). scale `"ordinal"` `"continuous"`. continuous Settings continuous scores: `center` (mean score), `theta_sd`, `item_sd`, `severity_sd` `sigma` (residual SD), score scale, `bounds` (scores truncated range) `round` (round whole points). replace `theta_mean`, `theta_sd`, `item_sd` `severity_sd` `scale = "continuous"`. seed Optional RNG seed.

title: decisionfacets (development version)
text: Designs one examiner per case (partially overlapping rating design) now supported. df_counterfactual() compares candidate’s observed examiners random reassignments draw, case, examiner qualified case, without repeating examiner candidate. df_simulate() gains design = "per_item" raters_per_item. Continuous scores (example 0-100) supported linear many-facet model, score = ability - case difficulty - examiner severity + error. df_data() gains scale = c("auto", "ordinal", "continuous"); df_fit() uses new "linear" engine continuous scores; df_simulate() gains scale = "continuous". New decision rule df_cut(value, "raw_mean"): pass mean observed rating reaches value (e.g. 70), convenient candidates different numbers ratings. df_fit() stops clear message rating network disconnected, rater severities comparable. New synthetic data set oral_exam: 300 candidates, 12 cases, one examiner per case, 0-100 scores. Results existing crossed designs ordinal scores unchanged.

title: decisionfacets 0.1.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-10-07 Initial release. Many-facet Rasch rating scale model fitting via ‘TAM’ (marginal ML) built-JMLE (df_fit()). Explicit decision rules: raw total, fair average, measure (df_cut(), df_classify()). Counterfactual pass probabilities observed, average random rater panels, rater-dependence flags (df_counterfactual()). Attribution expected misclassification measurement error rater assignment (df_attribute()). Known-truth simulation (df_simulate()).
